title: Uniform reduction bounds for finite stratified perfect local models
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), and let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_X$. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on a pro-etale covering of each stratum $S$, the restriction of $K$ is isomorphic to $B_U\otimes_A^LP$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], a bounded complex of finite projective modules, which may vary with the covering member $U$; here $B_U=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_U$. Then there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ and $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/I^n)_X)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, simultaneously for all $n\ge1$. For each $n,q$ the latter cohomology sheaf is intrinsically constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]; on the given strata its restrictions have constant finite $(A/I^n)$-module models on the chosen covers. No completeness or compatible etale-origin witnesses are asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.6.10(1); Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication, finite bounds and finite-level constructibility

proof.text: For each original covering member $U\to S_\alpha$, choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P_U^\bullet$ of its perfect scalar model, with terms zero outside $[a_U,b_U]$. A finite generating set gives a surjection $A^{r}\to P_U^j$, which splits by projectivity. Applying constants and then extension to $B_U$ preserves the two splitting maps and their identity composite. Thus $\underline{P_U^j}$ and $B_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_U^j}$ are retracts of finite free sheaves over their respective coefficient rings. Tensoring with such a retract preserves injections, because tensor with the finite free sheaf is a finite direct sum of the identity. Both bounded complexes are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Consequently the local model $B_U\otimes_A^LP_U$ is represented by $M_U^\bullet=B_U\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_U^\bullet}$, zero outside the same interval. In particular its cohomology vanishes outside that interval.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; Tags 06YT and 06YU, computation of derived change of rings by K-flat representatives

proof.text: Write $R_n=(A/I^n)_X$ and $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_X}R_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stratum-completion-unit-restriction] to each composite $U\to S_\alpha\to X$. Its coefficient identifications give $B_X|_U\cong B_U$ and $R_n|_U\cong(A/I^n)_U$ and identify $K_n|_U$ with $(K|_U)\otimes^L_{B_U}(A/I^n)_U$. Use the given local-model isomorphism for $K|_U$. The same cited statement makes these inverse images exact on modules. Therefore they commute with cohomology: apply exactness to the kernels of differentials and to the quotients of those kernels by images. These comparisons apply to both $K$ and every $K_n$; none uses a completion unit or a completeness assertion.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1), coefficient restriction and derived quotient restriction; Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication

proof.text: Compute the last tensor using the $B_U$-K-flat complex $M_U^\bullet$ of step 1, by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. In degree $j$ the balancing map is $(b\otimes p)\otimes\bar a\mapsto p\otimes\pi_n(b)\bar a$. It gives $M_U^j\otimes_{B_U}(A/I^n)_U\cong\underline{P_U^j\otimes_A A/I^n}$. To check invertibility, first take $P_U^j=A^r$, where this is the identity on $(A/I^n)_U^r$, and then apply the splitting maps of step 1. The formula commutes with every differential, since those maps are $A$-linear. Hence $K_n|_U\simeq\underline{P_U^\bullet\otimes_A A/I^n}$ for every $n\geq1$. All these complexes have terms zero outside $[a_U,b_U]$; deriving reduction introduces no additional degrees.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU, K-flat computation of change of rings; finite-free calculation and retracts

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact], constant module sheafification preserves kernels and cokernels. Applying it to the differentials and their image factorizations in the complex of step 3 gives $\mathcal H^q(K_n)|_U\cong\underline{H^q(P_U^\bullet\otimes_A A/I^n)}$. Each term $P_U^j\otimes_A A/I^n$ is a retract of $(A/I^n)^r$. The coefficient datum makes $A/I^n$ a finite set, so this term is a finite set. Its submodule of cycles and the quotient by boundaries are finite sets as well, hence finitely generated $A/I^n$-modules (the entire finite set is a generating set). These are constant finite models on every original covering member, for every $n,q$.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; coefficient finiteness assumed in def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stratified-local-cohomological-bounds] to $K$, the given finite stratification, its given covers, and the intervals $[a_U,b_U]$ from step 1. Keep the finitely many quasi-compact open subschemes $W$ selected from the covering members by that statement; their composites $W\to S_\alpha$ are jointly surjective onto each stratum. They form a pro-etale covering of $S_\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Indeed, an open immersion is weakly etale, and weakly etale maps compose [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. The space $|X|$ is Noetherian (the argument of step 6 from [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]), so every subset of $|S_\alpha|\cong|X_\alpha|\subseteq|X|$ is quasi-compact and $S_\alpha$ is quasi-separated. Hence each $W\to S_\alpha$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For an affine open $V\subseteq S_\alpha$, each preimage of $V$ in a selected $W$ is then a finite union of affine opens. By joint surjectivity, the images of these finitely many affine opens are exactly $V$. Let $a$ be the minimum of the lower bounds and $b$ the maximum of the upper bounds of the selected original members. The cited statement gives $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For every $n$, step 3 gives exactly the same bounds for $K_n$ on these same selected opens. For a fixed $q\notin[a,b]$, their exact restrictions of $\mathcal H^q(K_n)$ are zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] with these selected coverings to this abelian sheaf to obtain $\mathcal H^q(K_n)=0$. The selected family and $a,b$ were chosen before $n$, so this holds simultaneously for all $n\geq1$. If the selected family is empty, $X$ is empty and use $[0,0]$.

source.place: Lemma 6.6.10(1) and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication: finite-cover boundedness and stratified detection

proof.text: The minimal-closed-subset assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] implies the descending-chain condition for closed subsets of $|X|$: the family of members of any strictly descending infinite chain would have no minimal element. Thus $|X|$ is Noetherian. The Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset] makes every locally closed stratum of the given finite stratification constructible. Step 4 supplies on each such stratum a covering by constant finite $A/I^n$-module models for $\mathcal H^q(K_n)$; step 7 gives finite geometric stalks. These are precisely the clauses of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. On the empty scheme a partition with one empty stratum supplies its convention $N\geq1$. This proves intrinsic constructibility for all $n,q$ and retains the given covers as the local models asserted in the item.

Fix a stratum $S=S_\alpha$, put $F=\mathcal H^q(K_n)|_S$, and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point over $y$. The given cover is jointly surjective [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], so some member $U\to S$ has a point $u$ over $y$. As $\kappa(u)\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\Omega\neq0$, its spectrum maps to $Z=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, so $Z$ is nonempty. $Z$ is weakly etale over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ by base change [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Thus [lem-fix-weakly-etale-algclosed-section] gives a section, hence a lift $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ of $\bar y$. Pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar y$ that factor through $(U,\bar u)$ are cofinal in those of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]: $(V,\bar v)$ is refined by $(V\times_SU,(\bar v,\bar u))$, weakly etale over $S$ by the same stability. Hence $F_{\bar y}$ equals the stalk at $\bar u$ of $F|_U\cong\underline{H^q(P_U^\bullet\otimes_AA/I^n)}$ (step 4). By [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk], this stalk is the finite module $H^q(P_U^\bullet\otimes_AA/I^n)$. So every geometric stalk of $F$ is finite.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication (locally constant with finite values); stalks along a lift of the geometric point to a covering member
